'''Raymond William Ogden''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 19 September 1943) is a British [[applied mathematics|applied]] [[mathematician]]. He is the [[Professor of Mathematics (Glasgow)|George Sinclair Professor of Mathematics]] at the Department of Mathematics and Statistics of the [[University of Glasgow]].<ref name="FRS" />

==Education==
Ogden earned his BA and PhD degrees from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1970, under the supervision of [[Rodney  Hill]]. His thesis was entitled ''On Constitutive Relations for Elastic and Plastic Materials''.<ref name="GNP" />

== Work ==
Ogden's research has been focused on the [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear]] theory of [[elasticity (physics)|elasticity]] and its applications. His theoretical contributions include the derivation of exact solutions of nonlinear [[boundary value problem]]s, for both [[Compressibility|compressible and incompressible]] materials, and an analysis of the linear and nonlinear [[Stability theory|stability]] of pre-stressed bodies and related studies of [[Linear elasticity|elastic]] wave propagation.<ref name="FRS" />

In the field of applications, Ogden worked on modelling the elastic and inelastic behaviour of rubber-like solids. He has also made contributions to the [[biomechanics]] of [[soft tissue|soft biological tissue]]s, the [[electroelasticity]] and [[magnetoelasticity]] of electromechanically sensitive [[elastomer |elastomeric]] materials, and the effects on [[residual stress]] in materials that are capable of large elastic deformations.<ref name="FRS" />

His book, ''Non-Linear Elastic Deformations'', published in 1984 and reissued in 1999, has become a standard reference in this branch of [[solid mechanics]].<ref name="FRS" />

== Awards and honours ==
Ogden was awarded the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers|ASME]] [[Koiter Medal]] in 2005 and the [[Prager Medal]] of the [[Society of Engineering Science]] in 2010. He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2006|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2006]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/raymond-ogden-12018|title=Raymond Ogden|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." {{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220093712/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=20 February 2016 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In 2016, the [[ASME|American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME)]] awarded Ogden the  [[Timoshenko Medal]].<ref name="Timoshenko">{{Cite web |url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mathematicsstatistics/about/studentstaff/newsletters/august16/headline_480715_en.html |title=Professor Ogden awarded the Timoshenko Medal |access-date=16 November 2017 |archive-date=17 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171117064751/https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mathematicsstatistics/about/studentstaff/newsletters/august16/headline_480715_en.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
